name: Mount Sharp Boxwork Ridges
finding: Observed crisscrossing 1–2 m tall mineral-cemented ridges spanning 10–20 km on Mount Sharp; interpreted as ancient groundwater-deposited mineral veins exposed after softer surrounding rock eroded.

source.title: NASA Mars Exploration — Curiosity Rover & Mount Sharp Boxwork

limitations: Exact pixel coordinates on the active local raster are unavailable until public/data/manifest.json is finalized.
Ancient groundwater evidence does not establish current liquid water.

name: Vera Rubin Ridge Hematite & Calcium Sulfate Veins
finding: Measured stratified sedimentary rocks with hematite and calcium sulfate veins on Vera Rubin Ridge; interpreted as ancient lakebed deposits altered by multiple episodes of subsurface fluid flow.

source.title: NASA Science — Curiosity's Proposed Path Up Mount Sharp / Vera Rubin Ridge

limitations: Exact pixel coordinates on the active local raster are unavailable until public/data/manifest.json is finalized.
Regional ridge context does not establish an instrument measurement at a demonstration marker.

name: Mount Sharp Sulfate-Bearing Unit Transition
finding: Observed salty, sulfate-rich mineral strata above the clay-bearing Glen Torridon unit; interpreted as a planetary climate transition from wetter ancient lakes to drier, more arid conditions.
limitations: Exact pixel coordinates on the active local raster are unavailable until public/data/manifest.json is finalized.
Stratigraphic interpretation does not provide route-level hazard or traversability clearance.
